method: Computed with PyEphem for 40° N. Meteor shower peaks and rates: IMO Meteor Shower Calendar. Dates are UTC and can shift by one day where you live.

planets.name: Mercury
planets.text: before dawn, low in the south-east before sunrise; by the end of the period: hidden in the Sun's glare

planets.name: Venus
planets.text: before dawn, midway up in the south-east before sunrise

planets.name: Mars
planets.text: before dawn, high in the south before sunrise; by the end of the period: before dawn, high in the south-west before sunrise

planets.name: Jupiter
planets.text: before dawn, high in the south before sunrise; by the end of the period: before dawn, high in the south-west before sunrise

planets.name: Saturn
planets.text: evening, midway up in the south-east after sunset

events.name: First quarter
events.text: First quarter Moon: half lit in the evening, the best phase to see craters with binoculars.

events.name: Leonids meteor shower peak
events.text: Leonids peak: up to 15 meteors an hour under a perfect dark sky, debris of Comet Tempel-Tuttle. Moon 55% lit: some moonlight. Best after midnight.

events.name: Full Moon (supermoon)
events.text: Full Moon, 360,800 km away. A supermoon: closer than usual, so slightly bigger and brighter.

events.name: Moon near Jupiter
events.text: The Moon (60% lit) passes about 1° from Jupiter: the easiest way to find the planet.

events.name: Moon near Mars
events.text: The Moon (56% lit) passes about 3° from Mars: the easiest way to find the planet.

events.name: Last quarter
events.text: Last quarter Moon: rises around midnight, evenings stay dark.

events.name: New Moon
events.text: New Moon: the darkest nights of the month, best for faint stars and the Milky Way.
